probably most people have a Hollywood vision of gunshot wounds - they expect to see visible trauma and a violent reaction when the bullet impacts, screaming, etc., as well as big bullet holes and blood, however this is probably the exception, not the rule

depends where you get hit, but if it's in soft tissue, there will be no no visible body reaction at the time of impact and the person will not be thrown back at all - as a matter of fact, there have been plenty of people that have been shot that didn't know they were shot

as for bullet holes, you're simply not going to see them in a poor quality video, especially given the black blouse - the actual hole size would likely be significantly smaller than the dia. of the projectile because the fibers would begin to unravel and cover part of the hole very quickly

If I had to organize internet culture into distinct eras, I'd divide them as follows:

  • Prior to 1995 - Prehistory.
  • 1995 to 2001 - The AOL Era, when emails and websites transitioned from luxuries to necessities. Google rises to power.
  • 2001 to 2006 - Web 2.0 Era. User content and input became key, from Newgrounds to Wikipedia, and social networks began to become important. However, participation was still far from ubiquitous, especially among older people.
  • 2007 to Present - Modern Internet, when everyone's mother is on Facebook. Even those who do not consider themselves at all tech savvy still influence internet culture via status updates and shares.

I feel that provided a piece of internet culture is from before 2007 or so, it is a remnant of a lost era. Especially since last year's novelties are already ancient.
